messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test method testReflectionLongArrayArray creates a two-dimensional long array and converts it to a string using the helper method toBaseString, which returns a base string representing the object's class name and identity hash code (not the full reflection string). The test then sets the array to null and validates the null state of some registry related to ToStringStyle. 

The current bug report points out that the ToStringStyle class uses a ThreadLocal internally which is created but never removed. This lack of removal causes the ThreadLocal to hold onto references indefinitely, leading to memory leaks in container environments when web applications reload. This bug is related to the lifecycle of objects used during reflection-based string building.

Given the test involves reflection to string functionality and the bug report highlights leaks due to ThreadLocals in ToStringStyle, it is likely that the underlying ReflectionToStringBuilder and ToStringStyle usage in such reflective toString operations are implicated. The test might indirectly cause the ThreadLocal in ToStringStyle to be created and leak memory since no cleanup API exists.

Recent bug reports are about unrelated issues (reflectionAppend copying excludes, javadoc, API docs) and do not provide additional context here.

The root cause is that the ThreadLocal instance inside ToStringStyle is never cleared, causing strong references to accumulate and never release, causing memory leaks especially in container environments with class unloading and web app reloads.

This explains the failure as it is related to resource (ThreadLocal) handling in the reflection-based string builders. The test indirectly triggers loading ToStringStyle classes and leaking ThreadLocals. The lack of cleanup API in ToStringStyle is the source of the problem.

Next, we should inspect the ToStringStyle class implementation to confirm the usage of a ThreadLocal, its lifecycle, and absence of removal or cleanup APIs.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
